term.def: AI governance is the set of rules and checks a company uses to make sure AI tools are used safely, fairly and within the law.

prompt.prompt: Create a 3-month AI skills plan for my [team or department], covering practical tools, weekly tasks and clear career milestones.

quiz.q: Moneycontrol reports that IT firms are beating low expectations as their AI business starts to pay.
quiz.why: This directly restates the Moneycontrol headline about IT firms and AI revenue.

quiz.q: ETHRWorld reports that India's tech workforce wants practical AI skills and clearer career paths at work.
quiz.why: This directly restates the ETHRWorld headline about workforce demand for AI skills.

quiz.q: AI systems can become completely free of bias if you just feed them enough data.
quiz.why: Bias often comes from how data was collected or labelled, not just its volume, so more data alone does not fix it.

quiz.q: Removing sensitive personal details before feeding data into an AI tool lowers your privacy risk.
quiz.why: Less sensitive input means less chance of that data being exposed or misused later.

quiz.q: Only large companies need written rules about how staff can use AI tools.
quiz.why: Small teams face the same risks of data leaks and errors, so clear AI rules help companies of any size.
